chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Hareez, from Zurara who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Investigation (tahkharri) always suffices when the direction of the Qibla is not known.'

key_terms.التحري: Tahkharri — the act of careful investigation and estimation to determine the Qibla direction when it is unknown. It implies due diligence and sincere effort.
key_terms.وجه القبلة: The direction of the Qibla — the direction toward the Ka'ba in Mecca, which Muslims face during salat
key_terms.يجزئ: Suffices, is legally adequate — a fiqhi term indicating that the action fulfills the religious obligation

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do when they do not know the direction of the Qibla for prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) rules that when a Muslim is unable to determine the direction of the Qibla with certainty, performing a sincere investigation and estimating the direction (tahkharri) is always legally sufficient. This ruling addresses the practical situation of travelers or those in unfamiliar environments who cannot determine the Qibla through normal means. The Imam's use of 'always' (abadan) indicates this is a permanent dispensation, not a one-time exception.
